title: Design current: what the circuit really draws
oneLine: The cable carries what the load draws from the supply, so Ib comes from the input, not the output: P ÷ (√3 × UL × efficiency × power factor), at the voltage actually at the board, with diversity only as guidance.
skill: Find Ib for single- and three-phase loads from a nameplate, with power factor, efficiency and a sub-board voltage; know diversity is guidance; work the showroom motor's Ib and its delta winding current.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 (J/507/9710), checklist in eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8 and QM Issue 1.3 p.13: 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 4.1

eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.3-4 (Q4a: 11 kW 400 V motor, pf 0.8, 86%; Ib 23.08 A computed; winding current in delta 13.33 A worked from the shown 23.08 A, 13.32 A unrounded)

title: Maximum demand: what the whole building draws
oneLine: Maximum demand sizes the supply and every submain; diversity is common-sense guidance from the On-Site Guide, not a rule, and balancing loads across the three phases keeps the neutral current down.
skill: Add up a board's connected load from the luminaire key, apply diversity as guidance, balance circuits across L1 to L3, and estimate the showroom's maximum demand with the motor.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 checklist (eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8; QM p.13): 1.1, 2.3, 2.4, 4.1

title: Device and cable: Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz, the factors and overload
oneLine: Each rating factor is heat the table did not allow for, so It = In ÷ (the factors that act together), and the worst section sets the cable; a device may let about 1.45 In flow before it opens, so I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz, which is why a rewireable fuse needs Cf = 0.725.
skill: Choose In and the device type for a starting current; apply Ca, Cg, Ci and Cf only where they act together and pick the governing reference method and CSA; check I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz and derive Cf; know when lightly loaded cables leave Cg.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 checklist (eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8; QM p.13): 2.2, 3.0, 4.1, 4.2
materialRefs: eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.3 (20 °C), p.4 (Q4b: 90 °C singles in conduit, delta running conditions)
practice papers: P1 p.2 Q1, P2 p.2 Q1, P3 p.2 Q1 (Section A (b)-(f)); P1 p.18 Q10b (lightly loaded cables); P3 p.3 Q3b (a hazard of overload), Q3c (wiring system considerations)
picture: Two pictures: the cable run in sections (the slides' 3 kW heater clipped, in trunking with another circuit, through insulation; 21.28 A and 19.34 A, the worst outlined), then why piece A, two marks on one current line (the device's I2 and the cable's 1.45 Iz; a rewireable fuse's mark passes the cable's in red until Cf = 0.725 pulls it back: 14.50 A, 18.85 A, 13.79 A, 20.00 A).

title: A neutral that carries more than the line
oneLine: Balanced fundamentals cancel in the neutral but third harmonics on the three lines are in step and add, so above about a third the neutral current, 3 × h × IL, sets the cable; only when the maker's data gives a harmonic figure.
skill: Use Table 4Aa's bands, compute Ibn = 3 × h × IL, decide whether line or neutral current is Ib, and apply the 0.86 factor.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 checklist (eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8; QM p.13): 2.3, 3.0, 4.1
materialRefs: case.json lesson 4 (157.50 A; 304.50 A; showroom harmonic figure to research)
picture: Why piece B: three line-current waves and their neutral sum; drag third-harmonic content from 0 to 60% and the neutral bar overtakes the line bar near a third, with Table 4Aa's four bands on the slider.
builds_on: AC circuits lesson 10 (balanced neutral current is zero)

title: Voltage drop from the intake, refined
oneLine: Voltage drop is mV/A/m × Ib × L ÷ 1000, added along the whole path from the origin and judged against 3% or 5% of the voltage you were given; a lightly loaded cable runs cooler (Ct) and, with a known power factor, only the parts of the r and x drops along the voltage count.
skill: Calculate the drop for final and distribution circuits, add the submain's (÷ √3 for a three-phase submain feeding a single-phase circuit), chase it to a compliant size, then refine it with Ct and the r and x columns.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 checklist (eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8; QM p.13): 2.2, 2.3, 3.0, 4.1
materialRefs: eal-l4-design-and-verification-spec.pdf p.37-45 (p.43-45 method only; the Ct and power-factor formulas to research)
eal-l4-project-presentation.pptx (pptx-pdf) p.6 (sum all voltage drops from the intake; three-phase to single-phase)
practice papers: P1 p.2 Q1, P2 p.2 Q1, P3 p.2 Q1 (Section A (f), (g))
picture: Two pictures: the voltage falling along the run from the origin through the board to the load, with the limit as a band (32.14 V failing 11.50 V at 85 m, 8.09 V passing in 6.0 mm²), then why piece C, a cooler conductor and the current at an angle (formulas to research).

title: Shock protection, and when Zs is too high
oneLine: Every metre adds to the earth fault loop, the loop limits the fault current at the lowest supply voltage (Cmin), and that current decides whether the device opens in time; when Zs is too high, a bigger cpc or an RCD.
skill: Calculate R1+R2 with the multiplier, Zs = Ze + R1+R2 (or Zs at the board + R1+R2), the fault current with Cmin, and check it against the device and the time; know the RCD and supplementary bonding routes when Zs fails; the EV points' design questions on TN-C-S.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 checklist (eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8; QM p.13): 2.2, 3.0, 4.1
materialRefs: eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.3 (TN-C-S, Ze 0.1 Ω), p.5 (Q6 EV charging)
eal-l4-project-presentation.pptx (pptx-pdf) p.5 (compare Zs with the device's maximum), p.9 (EV: RCD protection, PEN fault protection, load management)
practice papers: P1 p.4 Q2a, p.7 Q4d, p.8 Q5a-b; P2 p.3-4 Q2a, b, d, p.7-8 Q4; P3 p.2 Q2a, p.3 Q4d, Q5a-b (Zs; RCD when Zs is too high; Cmin; where ADS cannot be met)
picture: The fault loop: the earth fault path as a ring (Ze, line out, fault, cpc back) beside the device's curve; lengthen the run and the fault current's point slides from 0.1 s towards the time limit, then past it in red; a cold/hot toggle shows the multiplier.

title: Surviving the fault: heat, short circuits, breaking capacity
oneLine: A conductor can take k²S² of fault energy, so it survives if I²t is smaller: S = √(I²t) ÷ k for the cpc with I at Cmax, t = k²S² ÷ I² for the live conductors, and every device must break the largest fault (IPF ≤ Icn).
skill: Size the minimum cpc by the adiabatic equation; know suitable from minimum cpc; check live conductors under short circuit; choose Cmin or Cmax for each check; check IPF ≤ Icn; justify SWA armour as the cpc.
specRefs: EAL ED4-01 checklist (eal-ed4-assign-01a-learner-pack.pdf p.8; QM p.13): 2.2, 2.3, 3.0, 4.1
materialRefs: eal-l4-project-presentation.pptx (pptx-pdf) p.5 (thermal constraints; SWA armour as cpc justified by calculation)
practice papers: P1 p.4 Q2a, p.9 Q5c; P2 p.4 Q2c, p.9 Q5; P3 p.2 Q2a-b
picture: Why piece D: one Zs, two fault currents; two bars, the fault's I²t and what the cpc can take (k²S²); a Cmin/Cmax switch shows which check each one drives; then the equation turned round for a short circuit, and IPF beside Icn.

title: Verification and handover
oneLine: The design predicts the readings: a cold reading is compared after correcting it to running temperature, installed values usually come in lower, and the designer hands over what the inspector and the client need, with a first inspection interval from industry guidance.
skill: Predict the test readings from the design, compare measured readings with it and with the device's maximum, and name the designer's information for the inspector, the first inspection interval and the handover documents.

title: A second job: the lathe, start to finish
oneLine: A whole design in one pass on a circuit unlike the showroom's, then the cpc: the table's size is safe, a smaller one passes only if Zs and the heat check both still hold, and steel armour, alone or with a core in parallel, can do the job.
skill: Design a motor circuit end to end at a board below 400 V; decide whether a smaller cpc can be used and what sets the smallest; justify armour as the cpc by Table 54.7 or the adiabatic, alone or in parallel with a core.
